text:
pagerbot: ALERT 2361112222 - Severity: P1 - Multiple container restarts observed on serving-eu-west-1 for prefill path. Paging on-call.

deploybot: automated note: recent deployment 2026-03-15T09:40Z to runtime-edge-eu-west-1. No rollback detected.

alex: I'm on it. seeing repeated GPU OOMs on model rw-gpt-30b-ctx during prefill. GPUs hit ~98% mem then container exits (sigkill). first observed 09:42:11Z.

maya: attaching a log snippet from one replica: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:42:11Z] runtime.prefill: attempting alloc 350000000 bytes
[2026-03-15T09:42:11Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:42:11Z] runtime: killing container due to unrecoverable OOM
[2026-03-15T09:42:11Z] containerd: container exited with status 137
```

keiko: impact?

sam: CS shows three dedicated tenants with increased 502/503s, about 120 failed requests in last 15m. Also a spike in node flapping - orchestration restarted the pod twice.

evan: infra data: nvidia-smi snapshot at OOM time - GPU0+1 had used 47.9GB/49GB, processes pinned large contiguous buffers from prefill. I can provision a spare node in 5m if needed.

alex: quick hypothesis: new customer workload sending single-request contexts >150k tokens. prefill tries to allocate large contiguous buffers for KV caches leading to OOM. The runtime isn't doing graceful eviction and we hit out-of-memory kill.

maya: repro in staging with a 180k-token prompt, got the same OOM and container termination. Also saw NV driver report: "out of memory during cudaMalloc".

keiko: interim mitigations proposed:
- enable input-size gate at gateway: reject prefill requests >200k tokens with 413
- turn on split-prefill (chunked prefill) flag in runtime to avoid single huge allocs
- disable prefill kv caching for rw-gpt-30b-ctx route (falls back to streaming tokens)
- add auto-retry with exponential backoff in client path for transient 5xxs

alex: doing gateway rule now: "limit_prefill_tokens=200000" applied to eu-west-1 routes. Pushing runtime flag split-prefill=true to a single canary node.

sam: rolling canary accepted. canary metrics look healthier: canary node saw prefill attempts but used CPU fallback for the biggest requests and didn't crash.

evan: provisioning a hot spare GPU node and adding it to the pool to reduce pressure while we roll config. done in 4m.

maya: experimental patch tested: when CUDA OOM occurs, runtime will attempt compact-kv-evict then fall back to cudaMallocManaged (unified memory) before hard failing. in staging it reduced hard crashes but increased latency for those requests.

alex: canary result: after enabling split-prefill + compact-evict, OOMs on that node went to 0 for 20m. non-canary replicas still showing some restarts. beginning cluster-wide rollout with 1-min stagger.

louisa: customer comms: "We're investigating and have applied temporary mitigations; very large single requests may be rejected or slower due to fallback to CPU/host memory. We'll update once fully rolled." sent at 09:59Z to affected accounts.

keiko: logs show some CUDA errors with different signature: "CUDA error: out of memory (700) during cudaMemcpy", followed by containerd restart. NV driver preemption not triggered; it's genuine OOM.

evan: note: one node showed oom_kill on containerd process rather than the model process - suggests host memory pressure in addition to GPU. we should check host-side allocator.

alex: additional short-term defenses added:
- increase eviction aggressiveness: kv_cache_trim_threshold from 0.8 -> 0.6
- reduce max_prefill_batch from 12 -> 6
- add route-level max_tokens soft-limit of 120k with warning header for customers

maya: reproducible testcase saved in gist; minimal repro (different from typical):
```
# create long system prompt + huge context
python -c "import json,sys;payload={'prompt':' '.join(['x']*180000)};print(json.dumps(payload))" > big.json
curl -s -X POST https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @big.json
```

sam: customer question: can their requests be retried safely? My suggestion: yes if idempotent and stateless, but larger contexts should be trimmed. recommending chunked inputs.

keiko: plan for permanent fixes:
- runtime: graceful allocation path (compact-evict -> unified memory -> CPU prefill) and better partial prefill semantics
- API: tenant-level context quotas with client-side warnings and streaming-first default for >32k tokens
- observability: per-request prefill allocation metric + alert on contiguous alloc > 200MB
- perf: optimize split-prefill to reduce latency penalty of chunking

alex: postmortem owners assigned: keiko (runtime fixes), maya (tests & canaries), evan (infra autoscale & host mem), louisa (customer comms).

louisa: updated tickets and posted interim KB article recommending best practices for customers using long contexts.

deploybot: rollout log: split-prefill flag enabled on 8/12 replicas, compact-evict enabled on 4/12, full rollout progressing.

pagerbot: status - mitigations deployed, error rate decreased from peak 8% -> 0.7% for affected routes. paging: handoff scheduled in 25m from alex -> keiko.

keiko: taking over for oncall. I'll drive the postmortem and track action items. filing the incident doc and linking traces to the fix PR.

alex: leaving notes in runbook: "prefill OOM signature -> cudaMalloc fail + container exit 137 within 30s of request; check kernel logs + nvidia-smi snapshot; check kv_cache fragmentation."

maya: uploaded heap dump and nvprof traces to s3://redwood-incidents/2361112222/

evan: autoscaler kept buffer nodes for 10m after roll; I'll allow autoscaler to scale down gradually after 30m if stable.

louisa: final customer update scheduled after postmortem.

pagerbot: INCIDENT MITIGATED 2361112222 - follow-up: postmortem required.

keiko: post-incident TODOs assigned and ETA'd. thanks team for quick response. :pray:
